title: Temporary Works Design
seoTitle: Temporary Works Design | UK & International | Temporary Works Consulting
metaDescription: Fast, practical Temporary Works Design for contractors — calculations, drawings, design briefs and design risk, with reference to BS 5975:2024. Remote and project-based.
summary: Clear calculations and buildable designs for falsework, propping, excavations, hoardings, working platforms and more.
intro: Practical Temporary Works Design produced for the people who have to build it. Calculations are clear, assumptions are stated, and design risk is communicated so the site team and Temporary Works Coordinator can act quickly.

sections.body: Temporary Works Design covers the engineering of anything built to support the permanent works or keep the site safe during construction — falsework, formwork, propping, shoring, excavation support, working platforms, hoardings, crane bases and similar. The aim is a design that is safe, buildable and matched to the loads, ground and plant on your project.

Where temporary works are not fully covered by a standard manufacturer solution, or where there is risk to people, plant, the permanent works or third parties, a design and an appropriate check are needed. Most contractors manage this through a temporary works procedure aligned with BS 5975:2024.

list: Falsework and formwork support
Propping, needling and shoring
Excavation support and battered cuts
Working platforms, piling mats and crane bases
Hoardings and temporary fencing supports
Scaffold foundations and access interface checks
Temporary stability during construction sequencing

sections.body: Designs are issued with a clear statement of assumptions, limitations and the information they rely on. Installation, use and dismantling risks are highlighted so they can be carried into RAMS and the temporary works register. Designs are subject to project-specific information and an agreed scope.

title: Temporary Works Design Checking — CAT 1, 2 and 3 Support
seoTitle: CAT 3 Design Check Support | Temporary Works Design Checking | UK
metaDescription: Independent temporary works design check support — CAT 1, CAT 2 and CAT 3, with clear review comments. Requirements depend on category, complexity and client procedure.
h1: Design Checking — CAT 1, CAT 2 and CAT 3 Support
summary: Independent design check support with clear, practical review comments — at the category your project and procedure require.
intro: Independent check support for temporary works designs, with clear review comments and a focus on what matters on site. Design checking requirements depend on the project, temporary works category, complexity and client procedure.
deliverables: Independent review of calculations and drawings
Review of design assumptions and limitations
Coordination of independent checks where required

sections.body: Temporary works are checked at a category proportionate to risk and complexity. As a guide, CAT 1 is a check by a different competent person, CAT 2 is an independent check, and CAT 3 is an independent check by a designer not involved in the original design and from a separate organisation. The category for any item should be confirmed in the temporary works procedure and design brief.
list: CAT 1 — straightforward, lower-risk items
CAT 2 — more complex items, independent check
CAT 3 — complex, high-risk or unusual items; independent and separate organisation
Review of the design brief and stated assumptions
Independent verification or recalculation as appropriate
Review of drawings against the calculations
Comments returned in a clear, trackable schedule
Sign-off once comments are closed out

sections.body: Comments are written to be useful — flagging genuine issues, buildability concerns and missing information rather than noise. The goal is a design that can be issued and built with confidence, subject to project-specific information.

info: Designer's calculations and drawings
Design brief and assumptions register
Ground information where relevant
Plant and loading data where relevant
The required check category and client procedure

title: Crane Mats, Piling Mats and Working Platform Support
seoTitle: Crane Mat & Piling Mat Design | BRE 470 Working Platform Support | UK
metaDescription: Working platform, piling mat and crane mat support with reference to BRE 470 — plant loading, ground bearing and outrigger checks. Subject to site-specific ground and plant data.
h1: Crane Mats, Piling Mats and Working Platforms
summary: Working platform and mat support with reference to BRE 470 — plus a free online BRE 470 design tool.
intro: Support for working platforms, piling mats, crane mats and outrigger bearing, with reference to BRE 470 principles. A free online BRE 470 design tool is also available for quick, indicative sizing.
deliverables: Working platform / piling mat support to BRE 470 principles
Plant loading derivation from manufacturer data
Ground bearing checks against available ground data
Crane mat and outrigger bearing checks
Recommendations on material, testing and inspection

sections.body: BRE 470 is the established UK reference for granular working platforms beneath piling rigs, cranes and other large tracked plant. Support considers plant ground pressures, platform thickness, granular material properties and the underlying ground — all subject to site-specific ground and plant information.

list: Outrigger pad and spreader bearing checks
Crawler crane track bearing
Heavy lift load spreading
Edge effects, slopes and made ground considerations

sections.body: For early-stage and indicative sizing, the online BRE 470 Piling Mat Design Tool lets engineers and contractors enter plant and ground inputs and get a quick working platform sizing in line with BRE 470 principles. It is a practical aid — project-specific design must consider site, ground, plant and loading conditions.

info: Plant data sheet (track/outrigger dimensions, weights, loads)
